name: Acea Run Rome The Marathon
summary: Acea Run Rome The Marathon is a city-centre race in March. It starts on Via dei Fori Imperiali with the Colosseum behind the runners and finishes inside the Circo Massimo. The course is flat, but about 6 km are on cobblestones.
courseHighlights: Start on Fori Imperiali with the Colosseum behind you
Circo Massimo and the Palatino early in the race
Castel Sant'Angelo and Via della Conciliazione with St. Peter's Basilica
Piazza del Popolo, Piazza di Spagna and Piazza Navona
Last 2 km past the Vittoriano and Bocca della Verità, then the finish in the Circo Massimo

paceStrategy.summary: The course is flat. The official site gives a start height of 22 m, a high point of 31 m and a low point of 8.1 m. The main challenge is the cobblestones, so start steadily and keep your stride short on rough streets.

segments.terrain: Central Rome: Piazza Venezia, Palatino, Circo Massimo
segments.advice: Start slightly slower than goal pace, as the streets are busy.

segments.terrain: Lungotevere along the Tiber, then Castel Sant'Angelo and the Vatican (about km 17–20)
segments.advice: Settle into an even rhythm on the wide riverside roads.

segments.terrain: Foro Italico, Ponte Milvio, then back along the Tiber towards the centre
segments.advice: Hold goal pace; the course is flat here.

segments.terrain: City centre: Piazza del Popolo, Piazza di Spagna, Piazza Navona
segments.advice: Expect cobblestones in the centre; shorten your stride and watch your footing.

segments.terrain: Vittoriano, Bocca della Verità, finish in the Circo Massimo
segments.advice: Save a little energy for the final 2 km, then run it in.

fuelingNotes: Take gels on the flat riverside sections, before you reach the cobblestones in the centre, where it is harder to open a gel safely. The sources I used do not list aid-station positions, so check the official runner guide.
tips: Wear shoes with a little cushioning, as about 6 km of the course is cobblestones
Watch your footing on wet cobbles if it rains
The start is in the historic centre, so plan transport and arrive early
Sun can be strong on open stretches even in March, so consider a cap

faq.question: Is the Rome Marathon course flat?
faq.answer: Yes, it is flat. The official site gives a start height of 22 m, a highest point of 31 m and a lowest point of 8.1 m. A race guide says there are one or two short climbs.

faq.question: Does the Rome Marathon have cobblestones?
faq.answer: Yes. A race guide that is approved by the organiser says there are about 6 km of cobblestones.
